- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast to reflect downward risk.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in the next few days; apply a 1–2 day lag correction downward.
- If model forecast mean is > 10% above recent 7-day average, consider mean reversion bias; adjust downward by 5–10%.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “high-low” swings (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 1.00), model tends to overreact; dampen forecast volatility.
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast starts above 72.0 and true outcome drops below 70.0 within 5 days, reduce forecast slope; expect mean reversion.
- If sentiment includes multiple 1.00 values, model may overfit recent trends; apply smoothing or reduce weight on last 3–5 data points.
